title: Why Does a Week Have 7 Days?
lines: Why does a week have seven days?
Almost everything on your calendar comes from the sky. | Except the week.
A day is one spin of the Earth.
A month is roughly one lunar cycle, about twenty-nine and a half days.
A year is one trip around the Sun.
But nothing up there takes a week. | And twice, whole countries tried to abolish it.
One theory: each of the Moon's four phases lasts a little over seven days.
But historians trace the seven back to Babylon, where sky-watchers tracked seven moving lights.
The Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
Seven wanderers, | and seven became a sacred number.
The Jewish week, six days of work, then a Sabbath, | made seven a steady rhythm.
Christianity and Islam later carried it across the world.
Meanwhile, Roman astrologers gave each day to one of those lights. | The names survive.
Saturday is Saturn's day. | Sunday, the Sun's. | Monday, the Moon's.
French keeps the rest: | mardi, Mars. Mercredi, Mercury. | Jeudi, Jupiter. Vendredi, Venus.
English swapped in Norse gods: | Tyr, Woden, Thor and Frigg.
Revolutionary France tried a ten-day week in seventeen ninety-three. | It lasted twelve years.
The Soviets tried five- and six-day weeks. | By nineteen forty, seven was back.
Empires fell. Calendars changed. | The seven-day week outlived them all.
